notes:
CRM notes — shorthand, from calls and security thread. 
- Use case: customer-facing support agent + internal doc search for financial advisors; strict no-PHI export. 
- Deployment preference: Private VPC (customer-managed), prefer AWS PrivateLink over internet-facing endpoints. If PrivateLink not possible for specific region, Transit Gateway peering is acceptable. Lacuna: 'must not traverse public internet egress for PII tokens' emphasized by SecOps.
- Network controls requested: IP allowlist for egress to Redwood control plane, explicit firewall rule templates (ingress: none; egress: allow-to-redwood-private-endpoints on TCP 443), deny-all egress default, NAT gateway only for approved maintenance windows, VPC endpoints for S3 logging.
- Authentication & keys: require customer-managed KMS CMK in their account with grant for Redwood cross-account decrypt; key rotation policy must be documented.
- Audit/logging: send audit logs to their Splunk via S3 ingest; retention 7 years for compliance; need proof of immutable logs and access controls. Also want CloudTrail + flow logs delivered to encrypted S3 with lifecycle policy.
- Mutual TLS: Security asked about mTLS for control-plane connections and certificate pinning for PrivateLink endpoints. SE said Redwood supports TLS and can add mTLS in dedicated/private builds; need engineering confirm for mutual auth on current private offering.
- Data residency: Primary data must remain in US-only regions; any EU customer data must be routed to EU-resident instance — Lacuna legal will require data residency clause in SOW.
- Performance/latency: 20–50 ms p50 target for chat flows; burst to 500 rps for embeddings pipeline. They are cost-sensitive at scale and want Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization.
- Security review status: completed initial questionnaire (security team happy with SOC2 scope). Next: KMS design review (SEC-4310) and network topology signoff.
- Quote from SecOps: 'No unknown outbound connections. If Redwood needs outbound callbacks, they must go through our proxy and be logged.'
- Artifacts: initial SOW draft in Drive, security questionnaire answers in Drive, FF transcript linked.
- Open questions: exact IP ranges for Redwood private endpoints (we provided /20 ranges but they want region-specific prefixes), whether Redwood supports VPC peering in a multi-account landing zone with strict route table controls.
- POC notes: planned 2-week POC to validate private endpoint connectivity + KMS grant flow; success criteria: successful KMS decrypt from Redwood in customer VPC, and audit logs visible in their Splunk instance.
- Next meeting: security ops walkthrough scheduled after we deliver revised topology (target next_step).
